notes.title: New BIG update
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45078807/1083b59f2b53ba0de44b49e90a2cefce236539eb.jpg[/img]
It took a while, but the game is now better than ever.

Changelog:
[list]
[*] New achievement added
[*] Tosia and Bobbin's story updated
[*] Bunnies in the story tab now have their professions listed and a frame added
[*] The watch glows red when you run out of keys to wind up robots
[*] The watch now also shows how much time has been rewound
[*] A new Controls tab was added in the game
[*] Level and world markers in the menu now have a highlight
[*] Level name now has a frame
[*] Fixed a bug related to arrow key input handling in the first level
[*] When using the mouse to control movement, you can now cancel a direction choice and wait instead by positioning the cursor appropriately
[*] After collecting a story fabric, you can now click the background to close the screen
[*] Updated controller input for collecting story fabrics
[*] Mute button behavior in the settings has been changed
[*] In extra levels the hint button is now greyed out
[*] On level load the undo button is now greyed out during the first turn
[*] Updated the credits list
[*] Slightly tweaked level 1-12
[/list]

More fixes are coming soon. If you’d like to suggest any changes, feel free to post on the community tab or join us on Discord!

notes.title: Hot Bunny Fix
notes.content:
[list]
[*] Added automatic language detection when the game is first turned on.
[*] Collecting fabrics now does not require a level to pass.
[*] Fixed achievements related to collecting fabrics.
[*] Updated the mod.io API for sharing levels.
[/list]

notes.title: Demo Update!
notes.content:
We would like to thank all the people who played the demo and gave us feedback and those who visited our booth at PGA. Our backlog has grown a bit and we have a few more things to do before the full release. 
What we managed to do:
[list]
[*] we fixed the robot's blocking movement at some points in the game
[*] we optimized the number of elements on the map so that there will be a little more frames on larger levels
[*] we changed the position and visibility of the keys and the clock
[*] we improved Tessa animations
[*] we made a number of improvements to the settings
[*] we fixed copying of levels in the editor list
[/list]

We encourage you to play the demo create your own levels and give us more feedback to make the game even better.

Get ready to immerse yourself in a world where adorable rabbits meet the intricate art of puzzle-solving, all nestled within a charming steampunk-inspired textile business setting. 🏭🕰️

At our booth, attendees will have the exclusive opportunity to delve into the whimsical universe of [i]Clockwork Rabbit[/i] on the Android platform. Designed to captivate both your mind and heart, this logical puzzle game invites players to navigate through a series of meticulously crafted challenges, each more delightful and intricate than the last. 🧠✨

[h2]Interactivity at Its Best[/h2]
Our hands-on demo will give you a chance to experience the rich narrative intertwined with brain-teasing puzzles, all while enjoying the beautifully drawn steampunk aesthetics. 🗺️🔍

The OnionMilk team will be on-site to share insights into the game's development, the inspirations behind its unique setting, and tips for tackling its trickiest challenges. We’re excited to hear your feedback and ideas, which are invaluable as we continue to enhance the gaming experience. 💡🤝

Visitors who try [i]Clockwork Rabbit[/i] at our booth will also stand a chance to get exclusive merchandise and other fun surprises. 🎁 Don’t miss the opportunity to snag some delightful memorabilia to remind you of your steampunk adventure! 🎩🐇

[h2]Last words[/h2]
Join us at the [i]Clockwork Rabbit[/i] demo experience and see firsthand why this enchanting logical puzzle game is set to steal hearts ❤️. Whether you're a seasoned puzzle solver or a casual gamer, there’s something magical waiting for you at OnionMilk's booth. We can't wait to embark on this delightful journey with you at PGA! 🚀

Mark your calendars and be sure to stop by. Hop into the world of [i]Clockwork Rabbit[/i] and let your journey begin! We are available from 25 Oct to 27 Oct 🗓️. See you there! 👋

notes.title: How can I share my levels made in the editor?
notes.content:
In the following article, I will show you how to create a new level and how to share it with others.

The level list from the editor is activated by the pencil icon in the main menu.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45078807/9a94ce948f41bac267e81b995a096c18c5e55f3d.png[/img]

Then click on the icon with a + to create a new default level.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45078807/cf60801a52f7a973b6c604e6a7dfc93bf63c5e6e.png[/img]

Each level has 3 buttons. From left: delete, edit, play.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45078807/eae18378ef93bf05e03a5efb7d04b97c4516bc6d.png[/img]

Click the edit icon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45078807/a21f134940e55d9dea0eb3b8529b49b39a20afbd.png[/img]

Default level o always a small 3 by 3 map with a rabbit in the middle. Change the name (1) and save the level (2). After renaming, a new level file will be created without deleting the old one.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45078807/98322e1a47a4374c55a77493ad3f18d612209dc2.png[/img]

If you want to connect some mechanical elements, you need to lay them out on the map. Most often you'll be connecting buttons or controllers to other elements like doors or smoke.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45078807/49217ea4d1ff35cff1330f814efb52ba367e7cb3.png[/img]

To connect elements to each other, go to the selection tab (1) and click on the box you want to select (2). All elements that can be connected and are not connected are highlighted in red.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45078807/688293e5eaaaf83fba2ef543dc5f3852b303925a.png[/img]

When you have a button selected on the map, click the link button in the menu

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45078807/60c5890afcb57a755fa5477c5e441e2c5a81468b.png[/img]

When you click on the door it will color green to indicate that it is connected. To return from connection mode to selection mode, click the button again.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45078807/58eb7bfab156495db9d98073f7e872787c918fca.png[/img]

After you have created a level using the available tools, you should save it with the appropriate button.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45078807/2ca6723a74820243fcb66bff26671ea79f35cd8e.png[/img]

After saving, copy the level with the copy level button.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45078807/1f84f8e502d56fb82412973298cf70c460e67479.png[/img]

We can now back to the menu.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45078807/c75a7e7c6bc8622bc24696c1149b177507b38a38.png[/img]

Let's create a default map for ourselves and proceed to edit it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45078807/3e01b1df01162cd679111cb3e2fdf15dcd2a216a.png[/img]

Use the paste button to have the one previously copied appear in place of the map.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45078807/b6278f24c2d48b8ec313136241228c183efe5cbf.png[/img]

Such a level should be saved. Remember that maps with the same names may overwrite each other.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45078807/f7d6a7bf09fa482b532b03c8a4479b7c99e80d3a.png[/img]

[h1]For more advanced players - map format[/h1]

The next part is a little more advanced and is not needed for fun.
This is what the map file looks like:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45078807/357f6308521cfab52df39a3d83523a46eab028f8.png[/img]
1 height
2 style/rotation
3 field type
4 mechanism properties like whether it is enabled
5 connections between fields
6 decorations
7 name
8 map size
9 background
10 ground style
11 music
12 music stage
